title: Projection maps as a morphism of strict derived towers
statement:
Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R_X)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small sites [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Use module-sheaf unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], derived pullback $Lf^*$ and direct image $Rf_*$ with the canonical adjunction and projection transformation $\alpha_{E,P}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Let $P_\bullet$ be a strict inverse sequence of bounded complexes of finite free $R_Y$-modules, with chain transitions $p_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$ and compatible chain maps $z_n:R_Y[0]\to P_n$. Put $P'_\bullet=f^*P_\bullet$, with the termwise pullback, pulled-back transitions and maps $z'_n:R_X[0]\to P'_n$. For $E\in D(R_X)$ form $S_\bullet(E)=\operatorname{Tot}(N\otimes_{R_Y}P_\bullet)$ from a representative $N$ of $Rf_*E$, and $T_\bullet(E)=\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_{R_X}P'_\bullet)$ from a representative $K$ of $E$, using total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. These define objects of the derived categories of strict towers, independently of the representatives. Write $R f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ for levelwise total derived direct image and $L_X,L_Y$ for strict total derived inverse limit [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. There is a natural morphism
$$u:S_\bullet(E)\longrightarrow R f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}T_\bullet(E)$$
in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(R_Y))$ whose evaluation at $n$ is $\alpha_{E,P_n}$ under the canonical derived-pullback comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. It is natural in chain maps of the entire augmented tower $(P_\bullet,p_\bullet,z_\bullet)$. The induced map $L_Y(u)$ is a morphism of the natural Roos triangles, including the connecting square. Let $\zeta_Y:Rf_*E\to L_Y S_\bullet(E)$ and $\zeta_X:E\to L_X T_\bullet(E)$ be induced by $1\otimes z_\bullet$ and $1\otimes z'_\bullet$, using ordinary-limit coaugmentations followed by the total derived-functor comparison. For the comparison $a_{f,T}:Rf_*L_XT\xrightarrow{\sim}L_YRf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}T$ specified in [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison], one has
$$L_Y(u)\circ\zeta_Y=a_{f,T}\circ Rf_*(\zeta_X).$$
No ideal or completeness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Choose a K-injective representative $I^\bullet\to E$ and put $N=f_*I^\bullet$, so that $Q(N)$ represents $Rf_*E$ by the K-injective definition of derived direct image; $N$ itself need not be K-injective when $f$ is not flat, and this is never used. For each $n$ put $C_n=\operatorname{Tot}(N\otimes_{R_Y}P_n)$, $J_n=\operatorname{Tot}(I^\bullet\otimes_{R_X}f^*P_n)$, and $B_n=f_*J_n$. The bounded finite-free complexes $P_n$ and $f^*P_n$ are K-flat, and the tensor totalizations are the complexes specified in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]; the chain-representative clause of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows] identifies $C_n$ with the derived tensor on the $Y$ side and $B_n$ with the derived direct image of the $X$-side tensor. If the representatives named in the statement are different, the canonical localization comparisons transport these models and their maps, so the resulting tower objects are representative-independent.

source.place: Tag 0943, section-projection-formula (canonical map and representative comparison)

proof.text: Apply the representative-independent pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] to every $P_n$, transition $p_n$, and augmentation $z_n$. It identifies $Lf^*P_n$ with the termwise complex $f^*P_n$, and carries $p_n$ and $z_n$ to $p'_n$ and $z'_n$. Thus the $J_n$ form the strict augmented tower $T_\bullet(E)$ used in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0943, section-projection-formula (naturality of the canonical map)

proof.text: For each $n$, use the actual term maps in [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows] with $h=f$, $I^\bullet$ as its K-injective complex, and $F^\bullet=P_n$. They are maps $t_{I^a,P_n^r}:N^a\otimes_{R_Y}P_n^r\to f_*(I^a\otimes_{R_X}f^*P_n^r)$, with inverse maps $s_{a,r}$, and the displayed naturality equation for $t$ makes them commute with both differentials. Finite totalization therefore gives a chain map $\tau_n:C_n\to B_n$, inverse to the totalized $s_n$. By [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-totalization], the derived class of $\tau_n$ is the projection transformation $\alpha_{E,P_n}$, under the canonical derived-pullback comparison, and $Q(B_n)$ is the level-$n$ object computing $Rf_*T_n(E)$.

The naturality equation $B(u)t=t'A(u)$ in [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows], applied to each coefficient transition $p_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$, gives a strict equality of the bidegree maps defining $\tau_{n+1}$ and $\tau_n$. Since totalization is a finite direct sum in each degree, these equalities say that $\tau_\bullet:C_\bullet\to f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}J_\bullet$ is a morphism of strict chain towers. Define $u$ to be the composite in the derived tower category
$$Q(C_\bullet)\xrightarrow{Q(\tau_\bullet)}Q(f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}J_\bullet)\longrightarrow Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}T_\bullet(E),$$
where the second arrow is the canonical total-derived-functor comparison. For its evaluation, $\operatorname{ev}_n$ is right adjoint to the exact functor sending a module $A$ to the tower with $A$ at levels $m\le n$, identity transitions there, and $0$ above (exactness is levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]); so by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] it preserves K-injective tower complexes. Hence, for a K-injective tower resolution $j:J_\bullet\to J'_\bullet$, the second arrow is $Q(f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}j)$, and the evaluation identification $\operatorname{ev}_nRf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}\cong Rf_*\operatorname{ev}_n$ of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] carries its $n$-th component to the canonical map $Q(f_*J_n)\to Rf_*J_n$, an isomorphism because $J_n$ is K-injective. Thus the evaluation of $u$ is the class of $\tau_n$, hence $\alpha_{E,P_n}$. The construction is made before localization, so it does not identify $D(\operatorname{Tow})$ with $\operatorname{Tow}(D)$.

source.place: Tag 0943, section-projection-formula (naturality of the canonical map); chain-level tower realization

proof.text: For a chain map of augmented coefficient towers $(P_\bullet,p_\bullet,z_\bullet)\to(\widetilde P_\bullet,\widetilde p_\bullet,\widetilde z_\bullet)$, the same coefficient naturality of $t$ commutes with the map in the coefficient variable on every bidegree. Finite totalization and the canonical comparison to the levelwise derived direct image preserve these equalities. Thus the strict tower map $\tau_\bullet$, and consequently $u$, is natural in maps of the entire augmented tower. Naturality in $E$: a morphism $E\to E'$ is represented on the chosen K-injective representatives by a chain map $g:I^\bullet\to I'^\bullet$, unique up to homotopy. Naturality of $t$ in the module variable gives $\tau'_\bullet\circ\operatorname{Tot}(f_*g\otimes1)=f_*\operatorname{Tot}(g\otimes1)\circ\tau_\bullet$ termwise, and a homotopy $h$ between two such $g$ is carried to the homotopies $\operatorname{Tot}(f_*h\otimes1)$ and $f_*\operatorname{Tot}(h\otimes1)$, which the same equation intertwines. Hence $u$ is natural in $E$.

source.place: Tag 0943, section-projection-formula (naturality in the coefficient complex)

proof.text: The strict-tower homotopy-limit statement [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] supplies the exact functor $L_Y$ and its natural Roos distinguished triangle. Applying this functor to $u$, which is the image in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(R_Y))$ of the strict chain-tower map $f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}(j)\circ\tau_\bullet:C_\bullet\to f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}J'_\bullet$ of Step 4, gives the maps on the first and both product terms; the naturality of the Roos construction gives the commuting squares, including the connecting square. Therefore $L_Y(u)$ is a morphism of the natural Roos triangles.

source.place: Tag 0943, section-projection-formula (unit normalization and coefficient naturality)

proof.text:
The evaluation functor $\operatorname{ev}_1$ on towers is exact by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. The constant-tower functor $c$ is its right adjoint: a map from a tower $H_\bullet$ to $c(I)$ is uniquely determined by its component $H_1\to I$, since every $H_n\to H_1$ is the composite of the transitions. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes $c_X(I)$ K-injective, because $I$ is. No such claim is made for $c_Y(N)$: $N=f_*I$ need not be K-injective for non-flat $f$, and it is not needed. For a strict tower complex $H$ write $\kappa_H:Q(\lim H)\to L(H)$ for the canonical total-derived-functor comparison, natural in strict tower maps, and $\gamma_H:Q(f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}H)\to Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}H$ likewise; so $u=\gamma_{J}Q(\tau_\bullet)$ by Step 4. Put $\lambda_X=\kappa_{c_X(I)}:Q(I)\to L_Xc_X(I)$, an isomorphism since $c_X(I)$ is K-injective with limit $I$, and $\lambda_Y=\kappa_{c_Y(N)}:Q(N)\to L_Yc_Y(N)$, whose invertibility is not used. By the definition in the statement and naturality of $\kappa$, $\zeta_X=\kappa_JQ(\lim\iota_X)=L_X(\iota_X)\lambda_X$ and $\zeta_Y=\kappa_CQ(\lim\iota_Y)=L_Y(\iota_Y)\lambda_Y$, with $Rf_*E$ identified with $Q(N)$ through the canonical isomorphism $Q(f_*I)\to Rf_*Q(I)$. The comparison $a_{f,M}$ of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] is induced by the equality of underived composites $f_*\lim=\lim f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$, i.e. it is compatible with the canonical comparisons from $Q$ of that common composite to both derived composites. For $M=c_X(I)$ the common value is $f_*I=N=\lim c_Y(N)$ with $f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}c_X(I)=c_Y(N)$ strictly, and the canonical comparison to $Rf_*L_Xc_X(I)$ is $Rf_*(\lambda_X)$ after $Q(N)\cong Rf_*Q(I)$, while that to $L_YRf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}c_X(I)$ is $L_Y(\gamma_{c_X(I)})\lambda_Y$. Hence $a_{f,c_X(I)}Rf_*(\lambda_X)=L_Y(\gamma_{c_X(I)})\lambda_Y$. Naturality of $a$ along $\iota_X$ and of $\gamma$ give
$$L_Y(\gamma_J)\,L_Y(Q f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}\iota_X)\,\lambda_Y=a_{f,T}\,Rf_*(L_X\iota_X)\,Rf_*(\lambda_X).$$
The square of Step 7 gives $Q(\tau_\bullet)Q(\iota_Y)=Q(f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}\iota_X)$ under $c_Y(N)=f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}c_X(I)$. Applying $L_Y$, composing with $L_Y(\gamma_J)$ and using the displayed identity yields
$$L_Y(u)\,\zeta_Y=a_{f,T}\,Rf_*(\zeta_X).$$
This uses the coaugmentation of the constant towers; compatibility with tower projections alone is not used.
